title: Max Practices the Big Five
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: Max's teacher writes "The Big Five" on the board. "These are five ways our school stays safe in an emergency," she explains. "Every school in our county uses the same words, so everyone knows what to do." Today, Max's class is going to practice two of them.

First comes the earthquake drill. When the announcement says "Duck, cover, and hold," everyone drops under their desks, covers their heads, and holds on to a desk leg. Max squeezes under the desk, but Max's tail sticks out. The teacher smiles. "Tuck it in, Max!"

Next, the fire alarm rings. It is very loud, and Max covers both ears. "This is our fire drill," the teacher says calmly. "Line up, leave everything, and follow me." Nobody runs and nobody talks, so everyone can hear directions. The class walks outside to their spot on the field.

On the field, the teacher counts every student and holds up a green card that means "everyone is here." Max looks around and sees the whole school standing in neat lines, from the tiny TK kids to the tall fifth graders.

Back in class, Max asks, "What if the air outside is bad?" The teacher nods. "Then we shelter in place. We stay inside and have rainy day recess." Max thinks drills are a little bit boring, but Max also feels calm. If something ever happens for real, Max will know exactly what to do.
